:::{#thm-best-predictor}
#### Conditional mean minimizes squared-error risk

Let $X$ and $Y$ be jointly distributed random variables with $\E{Y^2} < \infty$.
Let $g^*(X) \eqdef \E{Y \mid X}$.
Then for any prediction function $g(X)$ with $\E{g(X)^2} < \infty$,
let $\prederr_g \eqdef Y - g(X)$ be the prediction error of $g$.
The squared-error risk of $g$ is $\popriskf{g} \eqdef \E{\sqf{\prederr_g}}$,
and it decomposes as:

$$
\ba
\popriskf{g}
&= \E{\sqf{\prederr_g}}
&& \text{(definition of the squared-error risk)} \\
&= \E{\sqf{\prederr_{g^*}}} + \E{\sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)}}
&& \text{(the decomposition, proved below)} \\
&= \popriskf{g^*} + \E{\sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)}}
&& \text{(definition of the squared-error risk of } g^* \text{)}
\ea
$$

Consequently:

$$\popriskf{g} \ge \popriskf{g^*}$$

with equality if and only if $\P(g(X) = g^*(X)) = 1$.
That is, the conditional expectation function $\E{Y \mid X}$
minimizes the squared-error risk among all prediction functions of $X$.

:::

::: proof

Write $\prederr_g = \prederr_{g^*} + \paren{g^*(X) - g(X)}$,
which holds because $\prederr_g = Y - g(X) = \paren{Y - g^*(X)} + \paren{g^*(X) - g(X)}$.
Squaring both sides gives:

$$\sqf{\prederr_g} = \sqf{\prederr_{g^*}} + 2\prederr_{g^*}\paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} + \sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)}$$

We compute the expectation of the cross-product term by conditioning on $X$.
Because $g^*(X) - g(X)$ is a function of $X$,
by @thm-cond-pull-out it factors out of the conditional expectation:

$$
\ba
\E{\prederr_{g^*}\paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} \mid X}
&= \paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} \cd \E{\prederr_{g^*} \mid X}
&& \text{(a function of } X \text{ factors out)} \\
&= \paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} \cd \E{Y - g^*(X) \mid X}
&& \text{(definition of } \prederr_{g^*} \text{)} \\
&= \paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} \cd \paren{\E{Y \mid X} - \E{g^*(X) \mid X}}
&& \text{(linearity of conditional expectation)} \\
&= \paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} \cd \paren{g^*(X) - g^*(X)}
&& \text{(definition of } g^*(X) \text{ and } \E{g^*(X) \mid X} = g^*(X) \text{)} \\
&= 0
&& \text{(evaluate)}
\ea
$$

By the law of iterated expectations (@thm-lie),
the unconditional expectation of the cross-product is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{\prederr_{g^*}\paren{g^*(X) - g(X)}}
&= \E{\E{\prederr_{g^*}\paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} \mid X}} \\
&= \E{0} \\
&= 0
\end{aligned}
$$

Taking expectations on both sides of the squared expansion,
by linearity of expectation (@thm-linearity-expectation),
gives the decomposition in the statement:

$$
\ba
\popriskf{g}
&= \E{\sqf{\prederr_g}}
&& \text{(definition of the squared-error risk)} \\
&= \E{\sqf{\prederr_{g^*}} + 2\prederr_{g^*}\paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} + \sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)}}
&& \text{(the squared expansion)} \\
&= \E{\sqf{\prederr_{g^*}}} + 2 \cd \E{\prederr_{g^*}\paren{g^*(X) - g(X)}} + \E{\sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)}}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)} \\
&= \E{\sqf{\prederr_{g^*}}} + 2 \cd 0 + \E{\sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)}}
&& \text{(the cross-product has expectation } 0 \text{)} \\
&= \popriskf{g^*} + \E{\sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)}}
&& \text{(definition of the squared-error risk of } g^* \text{)}
\ea
$$

Since $\sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)} \ge 0$, its expectation is non-negative:

$$\E{\sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)}} \ge 0$$

with equality if and only if $\sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)} = 0$ with probability $1$,
meaning $\P(g(X) = g^*(X)) = 1$.
Therefore, dropping the non-negative second term of the decomposition:

$$\popriskf{g} \ge \popriskf{g^*}$$

with equality if and only if $\P(g(X) = g^*(X)) = 1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-best-predictor-decomposition}
#### The risk decomposition in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor,
the constant prediction $g_1(X) = 3$ has total risk $5$,
which the decomposition of @thm-best-predictor splits as $5 = 1 + 4$:
the risk $1$ of the conditional mean plus the excess $4$ from using $g_1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-irreducible-risk}
#### Irreducible risk

In the squared-error risk decomposition of @thm-best-predictor,
the minimum risk

$$\E{\sqf{Y - \E{Y \mid X}}} = \E{\Var{Y \mid X}}$$

is the **irreducible risk**.

:::

::: {#rem-irreducible-risk}
#### The irreducible risk does not depend on the prediction function

The irreducible risk depends only on the joint distribution of $(X, Y)$
and not on the prediction function $g$,
so no choice of $g$ can achieve a smaller risk.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-irreducible-risk}
#### Irreducible risk in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor,
$\Var{Y \mid X = 0} = 1$ and $\Var{Y \mid X = 1} = 1$,
so the irreducible risk is $\E{\Var{Y \mid X}} = 1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-reducible-risk}
#### Reducible risk

In the squared-error risk decomposition of @thm-best-predictor,
the excess risk from choosing the prediction function $g$ instead of the conditional mean,

$$\E{\sqf{\E{Y \mid X} - g(X)}} \ge 0$$

is the **reducible risk**.

:::

::: {#rem-reducible-risk}
#### When the reducible risk is zero

The reducible risk is zero if and only if $\P(g(X) = \E{Y \mid X}) = 1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-reducible-risk}
#### Reducible risk in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor,
the constant prediction $g_1(X) = 3$ has reducible risk $5 - 1 = 4$,
and the prediction $g_2(X) = 4X$ has reducible risk $2 - 1 = 1$.

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

This characterization of the best predictor under squared error loss follows @hastie2009elements [Section 2.4, eq. 2.11].
The risk identity in @thm-best-predictor

$$\E{\sqf{Y - g(X)}} = \E{\sqf{Y - \E{Y \mid X}}} + \E{\sqf{\E{Y \mid X} - g(X)}}$$

shows that the total squared-error risk is the sum of the
irreducible risk (@def-irreducible-risk)
and the reducible risk (@def-reducible-risk).

:::
